answer.rationale: Competitor price cut creates immediate churn pressure on price-sensitive SMB accounts. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is ruled out: it demonstrated strong short-term acquisition but materially harmed 30-day retention, creating long-term revenue risk that conflicts with the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Referral incentives (memory_57) work well for established customers but do not address immediate churn among price-sensitive new/at-risk accounts. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to the SMB crisis. Simplified onboarding and activation messaging both have proven positive signals. Activation messaging (memory_91) showed +6% activation, +11% week-one engagement, and critically +1% retention lift—directly addressing both acquisition and retention simultaneously. Simplified onboarding (memory_31) improved SMB activation but showed -1% retention, which is problematic in a churn scenario. A standard experiment combining simplified onboarding with in-product activation messaging leverages the retention-positive pathway (activation_messaging) while testing whether retention gains hold under competitive pressure. This preserves the option to layer simplified onboarding later if needed, avoiding an irreversible commitment to promotional pricing that would cannibalize margin. The approach is conservative, evidence-grounded, and directly targets the retention metric that matters most right now.
